advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish a failed probe getter from a genuinely empty axis (surface a note/flag when a getter erred) instead of collapsing both to an empty default.
evidence: `def _soft(fn, default): try: return fn() except Exception: return default` — every getter degrades any error to the empty default
build_mapping_layer emits `"statuses": statuses` and `"status_map": {s: s for s in statuses}` from those possibly-error-collapsed values (mapping_probe.py:275-279)
No liveness signal (exit status / non-empty capture / 'probe failed' note) distinguishes an empty result caused by a failed getter from a truly empty axis
advisory.finding: The probe's per-getter fail-soft (`_JiraProbePort._soft` swallows every exception and returns an empty default) makes a permission/transport failure indistinguishable from a genuinely empty axis: a 403 on `statuses()` or `issue_types()` emits `statuses = []` and `status_map = {}` with no signal that the getter actually failed. The operator cannot tell 'checked and empty' from 'the check never succeeded'.
scenarios: Operator runs suggest-mapping against a project where the account lacks browse permission: getters 403, block emits empty vocabulary/maps, operator believes the project has no statuses/types
advisory.suggested_fix: Have `_soft` record which getters raised (or return a sentinel), and add `_honesty_notes` entries (or a non-zero/warning path) when a vocabulary is empty because its getter failed, rather than because Jira returned nothing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add the promised `_notes` entry for an empty vocabulary or correct the `build_mapping_layer` docstring to match actual behavior.
evidence: Docstring: 'Empty vocabularies carry an honest ``_notes`` entry rather than a fabricated value.' (mapping_probe.py:264)
`_honesty_notes(hierarchy, hints)` only branches on `if not hierarchy:` and `if hints:` (mapping_probe.py:307-316) — no branch inspects statuses/issue_types/link_types/priorities emptiness
advisory.finding: `build_mapping_layer`'s docstring states 'Empty vocabularies carry an honest `_notes` entry rather than a fabricated value', but `_honesty_notes` only ever adds notes for missing `hierarchy` and present `hints` — it never adds a note when `statuses`/`issue_types`/`link_types`/`priorities` are empty. The documented behavior does not exist.
scenarios: A reviewer or operator relies on the promised empty-vocabulary note that is never emitted

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Escape (or JQL-quote-escape) the issue-type name before interpolating it into the JQL string in `_transition_hints`.
evidence: `issue_type` is a raw name from `port.issue_types()` -> `t["name"]` (mapping_probe.py:267), which can contain arbitrary characters
advisory.finding: Issue-type names are interpolated unescaped into a JQL string in `_transition_hints` (`f'issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC'`); an issue-type name containing a double-quote would produce malformed JQL. The value comes from Jira itself (trusted, read-only path), so risk is low, but a name with a quote silently breaks the sample query for that type.
scenarios: A Jira project defines an issue type whose name contains a double-quote; the transition-hints search for that type returns nothing (query malformed), silently dropped by the fail-soft search_issues

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fake-port variant returning empty/no-hierarchyLevel axes and assert `hierarchy` is dropped and `_notes` carries the honest limitation.
evidence: mapping_probe.py `_honesty_notes` appends 'hierarchy omitted: no issue type reported a hierarchyLevel' only when `not hierarchy`
Fake port `_ISSUE_TYPES` always supplies `hierarchyLevel`, so `_hierarchy` is never empty in any test
test_probe.py asserts `layer["hierarchy"] == {"Epic": 1, ...}` but no test asserts hierarchy is dropped or `_notes` present on a Data-Center/empty response
ABSENCE: no fake variant returning [] from statuses()/issue_types()/priorities() to exercise the fail-soft empty-axis contract
advisory.finding: The fail-soft degradation path — empty vocabulary axes and dropped `hierarchy` with `_notes` emitted — is never tested. The fake port always returns rich data (hierarchyLevel present, non-empty statuses), so `_honesty_notes`' hierarchy-omitted branch and the empty-axis fail-soft contract central to the module ('fail-soft on EVERY external getter … yields an empty axis + an honest note') go unexercised. A regression that fabricates a value on empty input, crashes mid-probe, or drops the `_notes` entry would pass all current tests.
scenarios: A Data Center project where no issue type reports hierarchyLevel
A 403/permission error that fail-softs an axis to empty
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test with a second fake port whose issue_types() omits hierarchyLevel and whose statuses()/priorities() return [], asserting `hierarchy` key is absent and `_notes` contains the hierarchy-omitted note.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that monkeypatches build_probe (or its returned port) to raise and asserts exit code 1 plus the stderr guidance message.
evidence: _cli/__init__.py: `except Exception as exc: … sys.stderr.write(f"Error: could not probe Jira project {key!r}: {exc}\n" …); return 1`
ABSENCE: test_probe.py has no test binding build_probe to a factory (or port) that raises to assert `code == 1` and the stderr guidance
_cli/__init__.py: `except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError) as exc: … return 1` (read), `except ConfigError as exc: … return 1` (serialize), `except OSError as exc: … return 1` (write)
test_probe_write_preserves_edits only exercises a valid existing rebar.toml and asserts code == 0
ABSENCE: no test drives a malformed existing rebar.toml or an unwritable target to assert return code 1
_cli/__init__.py: `target = proj[0] if (proj is not None and proj[1] == "toml") else base / "rebar.toml"` then `if target.is_file(): …` else data stays `{}`
test_probe_write_preserves_edits writes rebar_toml before invoking --write, so `target.is_file()` is always True
ABSENCE: no test runs --write with no pre-existing rebar.toml to assert a new file is created with the mapping block
advisory.finding: The CLI probe-failure error path is untested: `_bridge_suggest_mapping` wraps `build_probe()`/`build_mapping_layer()` in a try/except that writes a guidance message to stderr and returns exit code 1. No test injects a probe that raises, so neither the exit code nor the operator-facing error message is verified.
merged_from: The --write error/exit paths are untested: `_suggest_mapping_write` returns 1 (with distinct stderr messages) on an unreadable existing config (`tomllib.TOMLDecodeError`/`OSError`), on a `ConfigError` from `_emit_config_toml`, and on an `OSError` during the atomic write. Only the happy-path write is covered.

The --write fresh-file branch is untested. `_suggest_mapping_write` selects `target = base / "rebar.toml"` and creates it when no project config exists, but the only --write test pre-creates rebar.toml, exercising solely the `target.is_file()` deep-merge branch. Creation of a new rebar.toml at the repo root (and non-editing of an absent pyproject) is unverified.
scenarios: Jira project key does not exist
JIRA_URL/JIRA_PAT unset or access denied at probe time
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch mapping_probe.build_probe to a lambda that raises RuntimeError; assert main([...]) returns 1 and capsys stderr contains 'could not probe Jira project'.
